applicability.when: An HTTP or HTTPS origin is being evaluated for crawler discovery.

requirements.text: Request the lowercase /robots.txt path at the origin root and parse a successful representation according to RFC 9309.
Decode the file as UTF-8, recognize user-agent groups, and apply matching and precedence rules from RFC 9309.
Report that REP preferences are not access authorization and must not protect secrets.

applicability.when: The target publishes crawlable resources for URL discovery.

requirements.text: Validate the sitemap or sitemap-index root, namespace, URL scope, encoding, and protocol limits against the Sitemaps protocol.
When discovery starts from a Sitemap record in robots.txt, parse its absolute URL and fetch that document before claiming sitemap conformance.
Use canonical, absolute URLs and keep last-modified data truthful when it is supplied.

applicability.when: The target can advertise machine-readable resources from an HTTP response.

requirements.text: Parse every Link field using RFC 8288, including multiple field lines, commas, quoted parameters, relative targets, and anchor context.
Interpret registered relation names and extension relation URIs according to RFC 8288 rather than a substring search.
Classify selected discovery relations as agent-useful under a separately versioned AgentReady Lab policy.

applicability.when: The user opts into draft DNS-AID evaluation for a public DNS name.

requirements.text: Evaluate the owner names, service modes, parameters, and discovery procedure from pinned DNS-AID draft-02.
Parse SVCB and HTTPS records according to RFC 9460 and reject AliasMode when the selected DNS-AID profile requires ServiceMode.
Require authenticated DNSSEC validation evidence rather than trusting an unverified AD bit from an unspecified resolver.

applicability.when: The submitted page has a meaningful Markdown representation.

requirements.text: When this profile selects Markdown, return a valid text/markdown Content-Type as registered by RFC 7763.
Respect HTTP content negotiation without changing the resource's meaning or returning Markdown to an HTML-only request solely because a test is present.
Include Accept in Vary when caches could otherwise reuse one representation for the other.
Check that critical headings, links, code, and factual text remain represented without invented content.

applicability.when: The target uses REP to communicate crawler policy.

requirements.text: Parse group selection and allow/disallow precedence with RFC 9309 before reporting the effective policy for a named token.
Version and cite the external crawler-token registry used for classification.

applicability.when: The publisher chooses to declare Content Signals preferences.

requirements.text: Parse only the pinned Content Signals vocabulary and allowed values, preserving the REP group context.
Report omitted signal dimensions rather than inferring an unstated yes or no policy.
Describe the result as a declared preference, not consent, prohibition, or verified recipient behavior.

applicability.when: The target sends authenticated bot requests and publishes verification keys.

requirements.text: Validate the directory representation, keys, identifiers, media type, and cache behavior against pinned protocol draft-02.
When signature verification is selected, implement RFC 9421 covered-component, algorithm, time, and key-selection rules required by the pinned profile.

applicability.when: The target intentionally advertises an MCP server using the evolving Server Card proposal.

requirements.text: Pin an exact SEP-2127 commit and validate only the discovery path, card schema, and media behavior defined by that snapshot.
Validate all fields required by the pinned card schema, not only a name field.
Resolve declared endpoints and authentication descriptions without sending credentials or invoking tools.

applicability.when: The target claims to expose an A2A v1.0 agent.

requirements.text: Validate all required v1.0 AgentCard members, including name, description, supportedInterfaces, version, capabilities, default input and output modes, and skills.
Validate each AgentInterface URL, protocol binding, and protocol version against the v1.0 definitions.
Apply the exact v1.0 schema and extension rules rather than assuming that any JSON object with three fields is a valid card.

applicability.when: The target publishes installable or retrievable skills through the Cloudflare draft.

requirements.text: Use /.well-known/agent-skills/index.json and the exact v0.2.0 schema identifier and document shape.
Validate each skill name, allowed type, description, URL, and sha256 digest syntax required by v0.2.0.
When a skill artifact is fetched in interop mode, hash the bounded bytes and require the declared lowercase hexadecimal SHA-256 digest to match.
Inspect archive metadata under strict size, file-count, path, link, and compression-ratio limits without executing content.

applicability.when: A browser runtime implements WebMCP and the page intentionally exposes tools through it.

requirements.text: Evaluate the exact API surface and Web IDL behavior from a pinned Community Group report snapshot in a compatible browser.
Validate registered tool names, descriptions, input schemas, and lifecycle behavior without invoking arbitrary page tools.

applicability.when: The origin publishes one or more APIs for discovery.

requirements.text: Support and interpret the RFC 9727 well-known resource and api-catalog link relation as specified.
Validate application/linkset+json syntax, anchors, link context, targets, relation types, and attributes under RFC 9264.
Require the API links and relation semantics mandated by RFC 9727 rather than accepting an empty or unrelated linkset.
Advertise and validate the RFC 9727 profile URI where recommended by the specification.

applicability.when: The target uses OAuth authorization-server metadata or OpenID Provider discovery.

requirements.text: Construct the correct well-known URL for the issuer, including path-bearing issuers, under the selected RFC 8414 or OpenID profile.
Require an HTTPS issuer with no query or fragment and exact identifier equality where the selected specification requires it.
Apply each required or conditional metadata member based on the selected protocol and advertised capabilities.
Validate endpoint URL syntax and security requirements without contacting or authenticating to those endpoints.

applicability.when: The target is an OAuth-protected resource that publishes RFC 9728 metadata.

requirements.text: Construct the RFC 9728 well-known URI from the protected-resource identifier, including its path when applicable.
Require a successful application/json response and validate the metadata object under RFC 9728.
Require resource and verify that it equals the protected-resource identifier used to obtain the metadata.
Validate authorization_servers when present; do not require this optional member for RFC conformance.

applicability.when: The service adopts the WorkOS-led auth.md agent-registration profile.

requirements.text: Pin an exact auth.md repository commit or released schema before validating /auth.md and agent_auth.
Validate the underlying RFC 8414 and RFC 9728 documents independently from the agent_auth extension.
Validate registration method identifiers, URIs, supported identity or assertion types, and credential lifecycle fields required by the pinned profile.

applicability.when: The target intentionally publishes an ARD capability manifest.

requirements.text: For ARD v0.91, discover the static manifest at /.well-known/ard.json and honor the ard link relation.
Require each entry to contain a valid urn:air identifier, displayName, IANA media type, and exactly one of url or data.
Validate against the version-pinned official ARD JSON Schema and its semantic constraints.
Differentially compare fixtures with the official ARD conformance CLI without making that external tool a runtime dependency.

applicability.when: The user declares a known x402-payable HTTP endpoint; inferred ecommerce status alone is insufficient in spec mode.

requirements.text: Pin x402 v2 and reject messages or headers that belong only to an incompatible protocol version.
At a declared payable endpoint, validate the HTTP 402 response and the complete v2 PAYMENT-REQUIRED challenge object, encoding, and required fields.
Stop after validating the challenge unless a future isolated test explicitly authorizes a fixture payment flow.

applicability.when: The user selects the commerce profile for a service claiming OpenAPI payment discovery.

requirements.text: For draft-payment-discovery-00, require HTTPS GET /openapi.json, a successful application/json representation, and a valid OpenAPI 3.x document.
Validate payable operation responses and x-payment-info against the draft's supplied JSON Schema and semantic constraints.
Label every verdict with draft-00 because later drafts may change path, schema, or extension semantics.

applicability.when: The target claims support for a pinned UCP date version.

requirements.text: For UCP 2026-08-25, require the top-level ucp object and validate its version, services, capabilities, and payment_handlers members according to the pinned schema.
Interpret the declared YYYY-MM-DD UCP version using the matching date-versioned specification and compatibility rules.
Validate declared endpoint URLs and service identifiers without invoking commerce operations.

applicability.when: The target publicly advertises the beta ACP discovery profile.

requirements.text: Pin the ACP 2026-04-17 beta schema and validate protocol name, current and supported versions, and date-version negotiation.
Validate api_base_url, supported REST or MCP transports, and the complete capabilities.services shape defined by the pinned beta release.
Label results beta and avoid certification language.

applicability.when: The target explicitly opts into AP2 compatibility or a pinned AP2 version.

requirements.text: Keep the A2A extension detector only in the 2026-08-28 compatibility profile and label it legacy v0.1 behavior.
A future spec rule must implement AP2 v0.2 mandates, roles, schemas, and security semantics from a pinned release rather than requiring the removed Agent Card extension.
